pageCache.pageTitle: Swanage Primary School - Welcome from the Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Swanage Primary School!
Dear Parents and Carers,
I would like to take this opportunity to warmly welcome you to Swanage Primary School. We are a school dedicated to developing the knowledge, skills and values our pupils need to lead fulfilling lives as global citizens of the future. At the heart of everything we do is a genuine care for every child, reflected in the strong, nurturing ethos you will find throughout our school.
Our aim is to inspire all children to reach their full potential—whether their strengths lie in academic achievement, music, sport, the arts, or talents yet to be discovered. We are a creative and inclusive school where children are encouraged to thrive, whatever their starting point. We promote curiosity, responsibility and respect, supporting our pupils to make positive contributions to their community and to enjoy learning together as they develop skills for life.
Central to our approach are our core values: Ready, Respectful, Safe. We support children to be ready to learn, respectful of others and their environment, and safe in all that they do. These values underpin our culture and help create a positive, supportive environment where everyone can succeed.
We want all children to leave Swanage Primary as confident, well-rounded individuals who are well prepared for the next stage of their education. We support them to make positive choices, build healthy relationships and become responsible members of society. Through our inclusive approach, children are treated with kindness, fairness and respect, alongside clear and consistent expectations for behaviour.
Our staff are committed to providing engaging and creative learning opportunities that meet the unique needs of every child. We offer a broad and balanced curriculum designed to inspire, challenge and excite, helping children to become confident, curious and resourceful learners. Learning at Swanage Primary takes place in a stimulating and enriching environment where children feel valued, listened to and encouraged to take an active role in their education.
We are proud to uphold the principles of the UNICEF Rights of the Child, recognising that every child is an individual with rights and responsibilities that should be respected and championed.
At Swanage Primary, the education and wellbeing of our pupils is our highest priority. Our dedicated and skilled staff team work hard to create a welcoming and supportive environment where children can flourish. We also value the important role that parents and carers play, and we look forward to working in partnership with you throughout your child’s learning journey.
We understand that children only get one chance at their primary education. It is both our responsibility and our privilege to make this experience the very best it can be. We are incredibly proud of our school, our pupils and their achievements, and we are honoured to play a part in this important stage of their lives.
Finally, we are proud and privileged to be guiding your child through this exciting first stage of their education, and we will always strive to ensure their time with us is happy, successful and memorable.
Adam Burt Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Swanage Primary School - Coastal Learning Partnership
pageCache.text:
Coastal Learning Partnership
Thank you for taking an interest in Swanage Primary School, which is a highly valued member of the Multi Academy Trust, Coastal Learning Partnership (CLP).
CLP is a single family of twenty schools across two Local Authority areas: Dorset Council and Bournemouth, Christchurch & Poole Council. The two furthermost points of CLP are Boscombe and Swanage. There are about 5,400 pupils overall who are supported by around 900 committed staff.
Our schools work closely together in a spirit of professional generosity and collaboration, sharing resource and expertise.
Although part of the same single family, every school in CLP is different and unique and those differences are greatly valued. Each school has its own identify and values which express the local communities that they serve. Those schools within CLP which are church schools express their Christian distinctiveness through their unique vision.
CLP’s motto is ‘Broadening Horizons Together’. This is because we want every member of the CLP community to really flourish; children enjoy an inspiring educational experience and staff enjoy professional opportunity and fulfilment. That is achieved through being part of a single learning community.
CLP has three core values which influence the way in which we work together:
Serve: Schools in CLP serve each another as well as their local communities and families
Inspire: Staff inspire each other and their pupils
Empower: Schools, and everyone in them, are empowered to be their very best
Swanage Primary School has made a commitment to the CLP family, secure in the knowledge that serving others in this way will lead to a better educational experience for all of the pupils.
If you would like to learn more about the work of the Partnership and its other schools, or to view documentation such as statutory accounts, please visit the Coastal Learning Partnership website.
You can contact Coastal Learning Partnership directly as follows:
Email: office@coastalpartnership.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Swanage Primary School - Inclusion and SEND
pageCache.text:
Inclusion and SEND
At Swanage Primary School, we promote high achievement for all and encourage all children to achieve their full potential. We are an inclusive school and promote equality for all.
We are incredibly proud of the relationships that we develop with each individual child which enables us to identify and address needs as soon as they arise. We offer extra support for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) and enrichment and challenge all.
Different levels of support can be provided depending on the needs of the child. Most childrens' need can be met through our Universal and Targeted Supported offer which is detailed in our Ordinarily Available Provision document available below.
Some children may require support that is 'different from or additional to' most of their peers and, if there are significant concerns around a child's progress, they may be added to our SEND register so that we can more closely monitor their progress and provide a more specialist package of support.
We aim to work in close partnership with parents to ensure we meet the needs of all children. If parents have any concerns regarding children's needs or progress, they should contact their child's class teacher(s) in the first instance. Information can then be shared with the SENDCo who has oversight of provision for all children who may in need of additional support.

Pupil and Sports Premium
Pupil Premium
Please read the information below which gives details of our Pupil Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.
At Swanage Primary School (SPS) we have high aspirations and ambitions for our children and we believe that no child should be left behind. We strongly believe that it is not about where you come from but your passion and thirst for knowledge, and your dedication and commitment to learning that make the difference between success and failure.
We are determined to ensure that our children are given every chance to realise their full potential. Pupil premium funding, along with allocations made from the schools own budget will help ensure this money is spent to maximum effect.
Pupil Premium Spending:
Our pupil premium money has been used to provide a range of additional support for our children and these interventions, along with quality first teaching have started to have a positive impact on children’s attainment and self-belief.
Through targeted interventions we are working hard to eliminate barriers to learning and progress. One of the schools aims is to ensure that ALL groups of pupils make good progress in order to reach age related expectations as they move through the school.
Targeted support is being provided through one-to-one and small group tuition in all year groups. Senior leaders also provide additional support through interventions/targeted learning. These interventions support children in knowing where they are and what they need to do to improve their work.
Information to be published to parents/carers:
In place of the current requirements regarding information about pupil premium expenditure, schools are now required to publish their Pupil Premium strategy. This should include:

How will the school measure the impact of the Pupil Premium?
To monitor progress on attainment, new measures have been included in the performance tables that will capture the achievement of pupils covered by the Pupil Premium. At Swanage Primary School, the regular cycle of data collection and the monitoring and tracking of the cohort’s attainment, will be used to inform pupil progress and enable the early identification of need, support and appropriate intervention. Review meetings will take place regularly throughout the year and will include members of the Senior Leadership team, teachers and TAs.
At each milestone, the school will review the impact of actions taken and will plan for how the funding will be specifically allocated over the next phase. When selecting pupils for Pupil Premium target groups, the school will look at all pupils across the school. There are some pupils who are not eligible for PP who will benefit from these groups if their needs are similar and we believe progress can be made towards individual targets.
Pupil Premium Funding and the impact of this is a regular item on Governors meetings.
